conventions.convention: Right censoring records U=min(T,C) and δ=1{T≤C}; Y_i(u)=1{U_i≥u}, so subjects remain at risk at their observed time. Event sums and products include u=0 and group tied failures.
The Nelson–Aalen integrand is zero when the risk count is zero. Empty event products equal 1 and empty Greenwood sums equal 0. Greenwood is undefined if a contributing Y_n−ΔN_n denominator is zero.
Survival means S(t)=P(T>t). For finite event-time support, the Nelson–Aalen target is the sum of discrete hazards, generally not −log S(t).

The continuous-time result assumes AC, no baseline event, an absolutely continuous event-time law on the horizon, independent censoring, positive risk support, finite compensator energy, and the common-filtration square-integrable martingale contract. Its limits are fixed-time limits.
For its convergence statement, Greenwood is extended by zero outside its positive-denominator domain; that extension carries no variance interpretation there.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the pooled Nelson–Aalen event-count/risk-count sum, Kaplan–Meier product, and Greenwood formula, with inclusive baseline endpoints, grouped failures, zero-risk branching, and positive Greenwood denominators.
For IID real observed times, the supremum over 0≤u≤t of |Ȳ_n(u)−s_0(u)| converges in probability to zero, and its expected square tends to zero, for every finite t≥0.

For IID independently censored subjects and a support point a_j with positive event and censoring risk probabilities, Y_n(a_j)/n and dN_n(a_j)/n converge to their stated probabilities, and the event-to-risk ratio, zero when its denominator vanishes, converges in probability to q_j=P(T=a_j|T≥a_j).

Under its stated continuous-time assumptions, Nelson–Aalen and Kaplan–Meier have the displayed subject influence expansions; √n(Ŝ_n(t)−S(t)) converges to N(0,S(t)²σ²(t)), and n times the zero-extended Greenwood estimate converges in probability to S(t)²σ²(t), where σ²(t)=∫₀ᵗλ(u)/s_0(u) du.

published_dependencies.used_for: The fixed-time estimator formulas are measurable statistics of the observed records.
Common laws and mutual subject independence in empirical proportion, uniform risk-set, and influence calculations.
Predictability of deterministic Borel functions and Borel transformations of empirical risk processes; product measurability for energy calculations.
Interchanging time integration and expectation in the subject influence variance calculation.
Identifying completed stochastic integrals with bounded left-continuous finite-variation integrals through deterministic step approximations.
Transferring the Nelson–Aalen terminal normal limit through g(x)=exp(−x), after separately bounding the Kaplan–Meier discrepancy.
Explicit ambient assumption inherited by the martingale integration and terminal influence-limit interfaces.

seams_checked.note: The estimator definition, consistency arguments, and example preserve U=min(T,C), event-at-censoring ties, and the distinction between censoring and truncation. Independence is explicitly assumed where needed.

The pointwise theorem explicitly assumes the finite-horizon martingale contract, verifies a simple pooled counting-process contract using absence of simultaneous failures, and establishes finite energy before applying the L² isometry. Its local step-approximation argument supplies the required pathwise identification.

The consumer first proves the random-denominator remainder and then verifies measurable IID centered finite-variance influences before invoking the terminal theorem. It does not infer a process limit.

The crossing-hazards example uses the group-specific product-limit formula with the correct risk counts. Its positive continuous event times justify the displayed (0,t] product, and censorings contribute no event factors.

The Aalen–Johansen algorithm uses the same inclusive risk convention and grouped all-cause product factors, including possible baseline events. It explicitly restricts the citation to the finite-sample formula and makes no borrowed consistency or variance claim.
